input:
Labeled defect
- root cause: The OR composition checks for retry_all when deciding whether to flatten an existing retry_any.
- failure path: with `(A & B) | C`, the retry_all on the left is spliced into the retry_any as if it were a plain list of predicates, so the combination behaves as `A | B | C`: a retry fires when only A holds although the author required A and B together; no error is raised and the extra retries are silent

Reviewer finding
- description: async retry_any.__ror__ checks `isinstance(other, retry_all)` when it should check `retry_any`. This is the wrong class, so it flattens the wrong thing.
- rationale: Trigger: `retry_all(a, b) | async_retry_any(c, d)`. The check matches and `retry_any(a, b, c, d)` is built, which turns an AND into an OR and silently changes retry semantics. Conversely, `retry_any(a, b) | async_retry_any(c, d)` is not flattened.
critique: The finding has the same root cause: the OR flattening check tests for retry_all where it should test retry_any. It also has the same effect: a retry_all's predicates get spliced into a retry_any, so an AND silently becomes an OR. The operand order differs slightly (reflected __ror__ on the async variant), but the faulty operation and the semantic failure are identical.
